newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela will privatize, no matter what - Poletto.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela will privatize, no matter what - Poletto.

text.p: Venezuela will privatise telephone company CANTV, as well as the iron and aluminium companies in Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana (CVG), despite the inevitable opposition, Venezuelan Investment Fund president Alberto Poletto said.
"We know that as we near the sales, enemies will begin to come out like the dead from their tombs," Poletto told reporters.
"But the government is committed to taking the privatisation process to its very end."
Union-based opposition party Radical Cause said Wednesday they opposed the slated November global sale of the government's 40 percent share in CANTV for the price of a "skinny chicken".

Their complaint followed analysts' estimates that CANTV shares are unlikely to reach the $4.71 sale price enjoyed during the company's 1991 partial privatisation. The telephone market is nearing saturation and the company's monopoly expires at the end of 2000.
Opposition congressmen have also voiced similar concerns over the sale of the CVG's complex of iron and aluminium companies, due to be sold at the beginning of 1997.

But Poletto said the privatisation of these three companies was the best possible signal of the country's serious intent to restructure the state and consolidate its economic reform program, Venezuelan Agenda.
"When we've done it (the privatisations), Venezuela will truly be in the big leagues," he said.
